D1-Q1.clarify: Distinguish the hybrid-set name from the number of orbitals in that set.
D1-Q1.connect: A change of orbital basis preserves the number of independent orbitals.
D1-Q1.way: Write one valence s plus n valence p orbitals; determine n and the resulting set size yourself.
D1-Q1.rule: For second-period atoms, one 2s plus three 2p orbitals gives four sp3 hybrids. The superscript counts p inputs, not total outputs.
D1-Q1.check: Changed check: an sp set has two hybrids because one s plus one p supplies two basis functions; use this conservation rule on the requested set.
D1-Q1.probe: An sp2 set is proposed to contain two hybrids. How many input and output orbitals should it have? Then apply your method to an sp set.
D1-Q1.pattern: Three for sp2, two for sp. Repeating the superscript-as-total rule in both cases suggests a held counting rule; correct changed cases after an isolated slip suggest an execution error.
D1-Q1.transfer: Give the input/output inventory for sp without copying the original set.
D1-Q1.wrong_idea: The superscript is the total number of hybrid orbitals.

D1-Q2.clarify: Separate a bonded-atom direction from the number of shared pairs.
D1-Q2.connect: The sigma component and pi component of a multiple bond connect the same atom pair.
D1-Q2.way: Circle the distinct neighbours of carbon, then keep an independent bond-component inventory.
D1-Q2.rule: HCHO carbon has three bonded-atom directions. C=O contributes one local domain, although its double bond contains one sigma and one pi component. Pi density is not confined to the internuclear axis.
D1-Q2.check: Changed check: a triple bond to N in HCN still supplies one C-to-N direction; carbon also has the H direction.
D1-Q2.probe: At carbon in HCN, count bonded-atom directions and C-N shared pairs separately. Repeat the two counts for HCHO.
D1-Q2.pattern: HCN: two carbon directions, three C-N pairs. HCHO: three directions, two C-O pairs. Repeated multiplicity-as-direction counting suggests the misconception.
D1-Q2.transfer: Explain why replacing a double bond with a triple bond to the same neighbour need not add a direction.
D1-Q2.wrong_idea: Each line of a double bond is a separate local direction.

D1-Q3.clarify: The task asks for a local count before the introductory geometry label.
D1-Q3.connect: Four bonding directions and no central lone pair use the demonstrated four-domain rule.
D1-Q3.way: Inventory only carbon-centred domains; attach the known rule without reading shape from page angles.
D1-Q3.rule: CH4 has four bonding domains, no carbon lone pair, and a tetrahedral introductory sp3 description. A Lewis layout encodes connectivity.
D1-Q3.check: Changed check: CH3Cl still has four bonded neighbours around carbon even if the bonds have different properties.
D1-Q3.probe: Count domains at C in CH3Cl and C in CH4. Does redrawing either as a cross change its count?
D1-Q3.pattern: Both have four; changing drawing placement changes neither connectivity nor domain count. Repeated drawing-angle dependence suggests a spatial-model error.
D1-Q3.transfer: Classify carbon in CH2Cl2 by domain inventory, not bond identity.
D1-Q3.wrong_idea: The page layout is the molecular geometry.

D1-Q4.clarify: Translate three bonds and one lone pair without adding a fifth direction.
D1-Q4.connect: Wedges and dashes encode depth; electron-domain geometry includes lone pairs, molecular shape uses nuclei.
D1-Q4.way: Make four labelled slots first; assign three N-H bonds and one lone pair exactly once.
D1-Q4.rule: NH3 has N at the centre, exactly three N-H directions and one distinguishable lone-pair domain. Tetrahedral domain arrangement and trigonal-pyramidal molecular shape describe different inventories.
D1-Q4.check: Count all four slots in the sketch; replacing the lone-pair slot by an N-H bond changes the inventory to an NH4+ teaching comparison, not NH3.
D1-Q4.probe: Draw NH3 and a tetrahedral four-bond NH4+ comparison. Mark which slot differs and recount the H atoms in each.
D1-Q4.pattern: NH3 has three H plus a lone pair; NH4+ has four H and no N lone pair in the local Lewis model. A recurring fourth H/fifth domain exposes representation substitution.
D1-Q4.transfer: Create an H2O domain sketch with two bonded slots and two lone-pair slots.
D1-Q4.wrong_idea: Adding depth marks permits an extra bond or domain.

D1-Q5.clarify: Choose a model by the output requested, rather than the chapter title.
D1-Q5.connect: A model has a defined prediction scope and unresolved questions.
D1-Q5.way: Compare each candidate against overall domain arrangement versus detailed orbital-overlap information; leave the choice to your answer.
D1-Q5.rule: VSEPR fits qualitative electron-domain arrangement. An orbital-overlap model addresses orbital participation. VSEPR does not itself calculate an exact experimental angle or full electronic structure.
D1-Q5.check: Changed task: detailed axial versus side-on overlap now requires an overlap description; a geometry-only account is insufficient.
D1-Q5.probe: Task A asks for atom/domain arrangement; task B asks which orbitals overlap along the bond axis. State what information each model must supply.
D1-Q5.pattern: A needs a geometry model; B needs an orbital account. Choosing the same familiar model without checking output in both cases suggests scope confusion.
D1-Q5.transfer: Choose the needed model when the new task asks for pi-overlap orientation in ethene.
D1-Q5.wrong_idea: A familiar chapter keyword selects the model.

D1-Q6.clarify: Use the stated internuclear axis to classify the overlap.
D1-Q6.connect: End-on and side-on are orientation/symmetry descriptions, not molecule-name clues.
D1-Q6.way: Locate the axis and the density above/below it; name the two classes yourself.
D1-Q6.rule: Sigma overlap is end-on/axial in the supplied sketch; pi overlap is lateral with a nodal plane containing the axis.
D1-Q6.check: Changed check: rotating the entire sketch on the page leaves its classification unchanged relative to the rotated axis.
D1-Q6.probe: Rotate the whole end-on sketch by 90 degrees on paper. Does it become pi? Compare that with rotating one p orbital relative to its neighbour.
D1-Q6.pattern: Whole-picture rotation does not change sigma/pi classification; relative orbital rotation can change overlap. Conflating page orientation with relative geometry suggests the misconception.
D1-Q6.transfer: Label a sigma component within a triple bond using its geometry.
D1-Q6.wrong_idea: Turning a drawing on the page changes sigma into pi.

D1-Q7.clarify: Identify whether the error is in connectivity notation or in its interpretation as physical shape.
D1-Q7.connect: A flat Lewis drawing does not assert that all nuclei are coplanar.
D1-Q7.way: Keep four C-H connections while assigning explicit towards/away/in-plane conventions.
D1-Q7.rule: For CH4 a wedge/dash projection represents four tetrahedral bond directions. Projected page angles are not all physical 109.5-degree angles.
D1-Q7.check: Changed check: rotate the paper or choose another viewing direction; the atom connectivity and noncoplanar model must stay unchanged.
D1-Q7.probe: Does a cross-shaped Lewis CH4 drawing assert square-planar CH4? Does adding wedge/dash notation change the number of bonds?
D1-Q7.pattern: No and no. Persistent inference from page angles to physical angles suggests a representation misconception.
D1-Q7.transfer: Explain two different projections of the same tetrahedral model.
D1-Q7.wrong_idea: A Lewis cross proves a square-planar molecule.

D1-Q8.clarify: The counting centre is nitrogen, not every atom in NF3.
D1-Q8.connect: Local domains consist of bonds and lone pairs at the selected atom.
D1-Q8.way: Circle nitrogen before counting; keep terminal-fluorine pairs in a separate inventory.
D1-Q8.rule: NF3 has three nitrogen-to-fluorine directions and one nitrogen lone pair: four N-centred domains. Terminal F lone pairs do not add N-centred domains.
D1-Q8.check: Changed check: substituting H for F leaves the local three-bond-plus-lone-pair N inventory unchanged in the introductory model.
D1-Q8.probe: Count N-centred domains in NH3 and NF3. Then state where the F lone pairs are located.
D1-Q8.pattern: Both N centres have four domains; F pairs are located at F. Repeated inclusion of terminal pairs identifies locality confusion.
D1-Q8.transfer: Count domains at oxygen in H2O while excluding electrons assigned to H.
D1-Q8.wrong_idea: Terminal-atom lone pairs add domains at the central atom.

D1-Q9.clarify: Critique the counting operation, rather than merely giving a corrected label.
D1-Q9.connect: Bond multiplicity and neighbour directions are different ledgers.
D1-Q9.way: Show the faulty ledger beside a neighbour-only ledger; complete the corrected count yourself.
D1-Q9.rule: Counting both C=O lines as separate domains confuses bond components with one bonded-atom direction. HCHO carbon has three domains.
D1-Q9.check: Changed check: HCN carbon has two neighbour directions even though C-N is triple.
D1-Q9.probe: A learner counts HCN carbon as four directions from one C-H line plus three C-N lines. Repair the operation and apply it to HCHO.
D1-Q9.pattern: HCN two; HCHO three. Repeating line-counting in both cases indicates the rule is held rather than a single arithmetic slip.
D1-Q9.transfer: Audit a proposed domain count for CO2.

D1-Q10.clarify: Map each set name to an orbital inventory, not its superscript alone.
D1-Q10.connect: One s plus n p inputs gives n+1 hybrid outputs.
D1-Q10.way: Write separate input/output ledgers for BF3 and CH4 before matching labels.
D1-Q10.rule: BF3: three domains and three sp2 hybrids. CH4: four domains and four sp3 hybrids. For these centres use valence 2s/2p language rather than ambiguous 1s + 2p shorthand.
D1-Q10.check: Changed check: sp uses two inputs and two hybrid outputs, providing a third case for the conservation rule.
D1-Q10.probe: Compare proposed totals sp=1, sp2=2, sp3=3 against basis-function conservation. Give the corrected sequence.
D1-Q10.pattern: The corrected sequence is 2,3,4. Repeating the shifted sequence suggests the superscript-as-total rule.
D1-Q10.transfer: Reconstruct all three set sizes without memorising the sequence.
D1-Q10.wrong_idea: sp2 has two hybrids and sp3 has three.

D2-Q1.clarify: Compare full local inventories, not only the common three sigma bonds.
D2-Q1.connect: A central lone pair adds a domain even though it adds no bonded nucleus.
D2-Q1.way: Make two columns: bonded neighbours and central lone pairs; connect totals to geometry yourself.
D2-Q1.rule: BF3 has three B domains; NH3 has three bonds plus one N lone pair. Introductory sp2/planar versus sp3-like domain/pyramidal shape follows the local model.
D2-Q1.check: Changed check: H2O and NH3 have different numbers of bonds but the same four-domain total.
D2-Q1.probe: Count local domains and bonded nuclei separately in BF3, NH3 and H2O.
D2-Q1.pattern: Totals 3,4,4; bonded nuclei 3,3,2. A repeated bonds-only rule differs from an isolated missing lone pair.
D2-Q1.transfer: Compare a four-bond centre with a two-bond/two-lone-pair centre.
D2-Q1.wrong_idea: Three sigma bonds always imply three domains.

D2-Q2.clarify: Conserve carbon orbitals while separating domains from sigma/pi components.
D2-Q2.connect: Three sigma directions do not consume the remaining perpendicular p orbital.
D2-Q2.way: Assign each carbon valence orbital once: hybrids to sigma, residual p to pi.
D2-Q2.rule: HCHO carbon has three-domain sp2 accounting, three sp2 sigma directions and one unhybridised p orbital; C=O has one sigma plus one pi.
D2-Q2.check: Changed check: for an sp carbon, two hybrids plus two residual p orbitals still total four basis functions.
D2-Q2.probe: Inventory sp2 carbon and sp carbon; can a p orbital used in a hybrid also be counted as a separate residual p?
D2-Q2.pattern: No double use. Totals remain four in both cases. Repeated totals above four indicate double counting.
D2-Q2.transfer: Inventory HCN carbon without copying the formaldehyde count.
D2-Q2.wrong_idea: A carbon p function can be counted in a hybrid and as a residual orbital.

D2-Q3.clarify: Construct the relation between the molecular plane and the pi orbitals.
D2-Q3.connect: Three sigma directions lie in each sp2 carbon plane; residual p is perpendicular to that plane.
D2-Q3.way: Draw both carbon frames, then align the residual p directions for possible lateral overlap.
D2-Q3.rule: Ethene has a coplanar sigma framework; the two residual p directions are parallel and perpendicular to it in the introductory model.
D2-Q3.check: Changed check: rotate one CH2 group while preserving C-C connectivity; ask which overlap is sensitive to the relative orientation.
D2-Q3.probe: Rotate the whole ethene picture, then rotate only one CH2 group. Which operation changes relative p alignment?
D2-Q3.pattern: Only the relative-group rotation changes alignment. A whole-page-orientation answer exposes a representation error.
D2-Q3.transfer: Sketch a qualitative twisted ethene comparison without predicting a numerical barrier.
D2-Q3.wrong_idea: Page orientation is the same as relative orbital orientation.

D2-Q4.clarify: The central carbon inventory must support two directions and two pi components.
D2-Q4.connect: sp accounting leaves two mutually perpendicular p directions.
D2-Q4.way: Allocate carbon basis functions and bond components in separate ledgers; keep the localized drawing explicitly a model.
D2-Q4.rule: CO2 carbon: two domains/sp, two sigma components and two pi components. A localized VB drawing is useful accounting, not a unique experimentally compulsory terminal-O orbital-plane picture.
D2-Q4.check: Changed check: HCN carbon also has two sigma directions and two residual p directions although its neighbours differ.
D2-Q4.probe: Give carbon orbital inventory for CO2 and HCN. Does a localized drawing uniquely measure the oxygen orbital basis?
D2-Q4.pattern: Both carbon inventories close at four. No unique O basis follows from the drawing alone. Repeated uniqueness claims expose model/observation conflation.
D2-Q4.transfer: State what CO2 geometry supports and what it cannot uniquely prove.
D2-Q4.wrong_idea: A localized CO2 drawing uniquely measures the terminal oxygen basis.

D2-Q5.clarify: Test whether three sigma bonds are sufficient for the proposed label.
D2-Q5.connect: A counterexample must hold the claimed condition while changing an omitted relevant condition.
D2-Q5.way: Choose a centre with three bonds and a central lone pair; test the claim rather than naming a familiar molecule only.
D2-Q5.rule: NH3 falsifies three-sigma-implies-sp2: its local lone pair makes four domains. Geometry constrains a model but does not uniquely prove a hybrid basis.
D2-Q5.check: Changed check: BF3 and NH3 share three bonds but differ in local lone pairs; the proposed rule predicts the same result incorrectly.
D2-Q5.probe: Would a three-bond nitrogen with a lone pair and a three-bond boron without one require identical domain inventories? Explain.
D2-Q5.pattern: No: four versus three. Keeping the answer identical despite the changed lone-pair condition suggests the misconception.
D2-Q5.transfer: Repair the rule with an explicit applicability condition.
D2-Q5.wrong_idea: Three sigma bonds suffice to prove sp2.

D2-Q6.clarify: Separate number of bonding directions from bond identity or strength.
D2-Q6.connect: Replacing a substituent changes chemical environment without automatically changing connectivity count.
D2-Q6.way: Recount neighbours before considering any unprovided property differences.
D2-Q6.rule: CH3F carbon has four bonding directions and introductory sp3 accounting. The count alone establishes neither bond lengths nor their detailed causes.
D2-Q6.check: Changed check: CH2F2 still has four central bonding directions; electronegativity is not an extra domain.
D2-Q6.probe: Count carbon domains in CH4, CH3F and CH2F2. Does each F add an extra domain beyond its C-F direction?
D2-Q6.pattern: All four; no. Repeated extra counting for F suggests property/count conflation.
D2-Q6.transfer: Classify carbon in CHCl3 without assigning an exact bond angle.
D2-Q6.wrong_idea: An electronegative substituent adds a domain beyond its bond direction.

D2-Q7.clarify: Keep local inventories separate from the triple-bond component inventory.
D2-Q7.connect: One bonded neighbour supplies one direction even when three bond components are present.
D2-Q7.way: At C and N count local sigma directions/lone pairs, then tally one sigma plus residual pi components.
D2-Q7.rule: HCN carbon and nitrogen have introductory sp local accounting; C-N contains one sigma and two pi components.
D2-Q7.check: Changed check: total valence electrons HCN = 1+4+5 = 10; the three shared pairs and N lone pair plus C-H pair use all ten.
D2-Q7.probe: Compare domain counts at C and N with the total number of shared pairs in HCN.
D2-Q7.pattern: Both local domain counts are two; four shared pairs plus N lone pair close the ten-electron ledger. Repeated multiplicity-as-domain confusion changes the local totals.
D2-Q7.transfer: Compare HCN and CO2 local carbon inventories.
D2-Q7.wrong_idea: Three C-N bond lines supply three C-centred directions.

D2-Q8.clarify: Count local domains and bonded nuclei at two different centres.
D2-Q8.connect: A lone pair contributes to electron-domain geometry but is excluded from molecular-shape naming.
D2-Q8.way: Use separate C and N inventories; do not carry a whole-molecule label from one atom to the other.
D2-Q8.rule: Methylamine C has four bonded directions; N has three bonded directions and one lone pair. Introductory tetrahedral C and pyramidal N nuclear arrangements differ despite four-domain totals.
D2-Q8.check: Changed check: replacing N-H with N-CH3 preserves the local three-bond-plus-lone-pair N inventory in the neutral localized amine model.
D2-Q8.probe: Compare local N inventory with carbon inventory in CH3NH2. Which centre includes a lone-pair direction?
D2-Q8.pattern: N does; C does not. Using one atom-global shape for both reveals locality confusion.
D2-Q8.transfer: Describe a neutral secondary amine N without predicting an exact experimental angle.
D2-Q8.wrong_idea: One whole-molecule label determines both carbon and nitrogen shapes.

D2-Q9.clarify: Avoid spending a carbon basis function twice.
D2-Q9.connect: For second-period carbon, one 2s and three 2p functions form a four-dimensional valence basis.
D2-Q9.way: Assign three hybrid sigma directions and reserve only unused functions for the pi job.
D2-Q9.rule: sp2 accounting is three hybrid orbitals plus one residual p. A p function already mixed into a hybrid is not simultaneously counted as an additional residual orbital.
D2-Q9.check: Changed check: sp accounting gives two hybrids plus two residual p; sp3 gives four hybrids plus zero residual p.
D2-Q9.probe: Build an allocation ledger for sp, sp2, sp3 and flag any duplicate-use entry.
D2-Q9.pattern: All totals four; residual p counts 2,1,0. Recurrent five-orbital totals indicate double counting.
D2-Q9.transfer: Allocate the sp2 basis without memorising an orbital picture.
D2-Q9.wrong_idea: An input p function can be spent twice in the orbital inventory.

D2-Q10.clarify: Test whether domain geometry and nuclear shape are interchangeable.
D2-Q10.connect: A lone-pair domain has no bonded nucleus to include in molecular-shape naming.
D2-Q10.way: Hold four domains fixed and vary how many slots are bonded atoms.
D2-Q10.rule: CH4, NH3, H2O have four introductory domains but tetrahedral, pyramidal and bent nuclear shapes respectively.
D2-Q10.check: Changed check: a four-bond/no-lone-pair centre cannot be assigned the same atom-only shape as a two-bond/two-lone-pair centre.
D2-Q10.probe: For four-domain inventories with 4,3,2 bonded atoms, give the atom-only shape and explain omitted slots.
D2-Q10.pattern: Tetrahedral, pyramidal, bent; omitted slots are lone pairs. Repeating tetrahedral for all atom-only shapes exposes the conflation.
D2-Q10.transfer: Sketch the domain and atom-only inventories separately for H2O.
D2-Q10.wrong_idea: Four-domain geometry equals the atom-only shape in every case.

D3-Q1.clarify: Separate supplied bond equivalence from a permanently chosen Lewis double bond.
D3-Q1.connect: Equivalent contributors are bookkeeping alternatives for one delocalised description.
D3-Q1.way: Compare what a fixed unequal-bond model predicts with the supplied equivalent positions.
D3-Q1.rule: Planar equivalent nitrate bonds reject one permanently unique N=O position. N sigma framework is locally sp2; equivalence alone is not the hybridisation criterion.
D3-Q1.check: Changed check: supplied equivalent CO2 bonds coexist with sp carbon; equivalence cannot alone imply sp2.
D3-Q1.probe: Can equivalent bonds at CO2 carbon and nitrate nitrogen imply the same local hybrid label? Recount directions.
D3-Q1.pattern: No: two versus three directions in these local models. Repeated equality-to-sp2 classification suggests the faulty criterion.
D3-Q1.transfer: Apply the distinction to supplied equivalent carbonate bonds.
D3-Q1.wrong_idea: Equivalent bonds are a permanently selected Lewis double bond.

D3-Q2.clarify: Translate formal contributors into one sigma framework and a complete pi-space ledger.
D3-Q2.connect: A formal Lewis double bond does not identify the whole delocalised occupancy.
D3-Q2.way: List the central and terminal perpendicular p contributions and preserve one set of nuclear positions.
D3-Q2.rule: Nitrate has three in-plane N-O sigma directions and four perpendicular p functions spanning a six-electron pi space. Contributors do not switch in time.
D3-Q2.check: Changed check: 24 total valence electrons = 18 in sigma/in-plane lone-pair bookkeeping plus six in the perpendicular pi space.
D3-Q2.probe: For nitrate and carbonate, count pi-space electrons including terminal perpendicular lone pairs. Do formal contributors describe alternating nuclear structures?
D3-Q2.pattern: Six pi-space electrons in each; no switching of nuclear structures. Repeated two-electron pi totals expose omitted lone-pair contributions.
D3-Q2.transfer: Translate carbonate contributors into a continuous p-space description.
D3-Q2.wrong_idea: Resonance contributors are molecular structures switching in time; only the drawn double bond supplies pi electrons.

D3-Q3.clarify: Assign local bases before deducing the relation between terminal planes.
D3-Q3.connect: A central sp carbon retains two perpendicular p directions.
D3-Q3.way: Match each central p direction with an aligned terminal p direction; infer terminal sigma planes yourself.
D3-Q3.rule: Allene uses terminal sp2, central sp accounting. The two central perpendicular p directions support perpendicular terminal CH2 planes in the introductory model.
D3-Q3.check: Changed check: looking down C=C=C, terminal CH2 planes project at right angles; rotating the whole model leaves that relation unchanged.
D3-Q3.probe: Compare ethene with allene: how many residual p directions are needed at the centre, and which planes must align with each?
D3-Q3.pattern: Ethene uses one aligned pi pair; allene central carbon uses two perpendicular p directions. Repeating a single planar p direction for both exposes the mapping error.
D3-Q3.transfer: Build the allene end-on projection from the two p directions.
D3-Q3.wrong_idea: All double-bonded fragments must share one plane.

D3-Q4.clarify: Explain the terminal-plane constraint using overlap geometry, not an invalid occupation claim.
D3-Q4.connect: Atomic basis functions participate in molecular combinations; Pauli exclusion is an electron-state rule.
D3-Q4.way: Name the two inter-centre pi overlaps and compare their directions.
D3-Q4.rule: Allene central sp accounting retains two perpendicular p functions. Terminal sigma planes are perpendicular to their respective p functions. Do not claim the first p orbital is filled by one bond and forbidden from multicentre participation by Pauli.
D3-Q4.check: Changed check: a delocalised nitrate p function participates in a multicentre description, falsifying the claimed one-AO-one-bond prohibition.
D3-Q4.probe: Does forming a pi contribution make an atomic p function unavailable to every multicentre molecular combination? Contrast allene direction constraints with nitrate delocalisation.
D3-Q4.pattern: No. Allene uses distinct perpendicular local p directions in its model; nitrate is multicentre. A persistent forbidden-reuse claim identifies the faulty warrant.
D3-Q4.transfer: Explain allene perpendicularity without using the phrase orbital already occupied.
D3-Q4.wrong_idea: Pauli exclusion forbids one atomic orbital from participating in any multicentre description.

D3-Q5.clarify: Evaluate bond equivalence as a criterion rather than as a conclusion.
D3-Q5.connect: Equivalent bond properties and local orbital-basis selection are separate statements.
D3-Q5.way: Test the rule on equivalent-bond examples with different central domain counts.
D3-Q5.rule: Equivalent bonds do not imply sp2: CO2 carbon is sp, nitrate N sp2, and NH3 N sp3-like in their introductory models.
D3-Q5.check: Changed check: CH4 has equivalent C-H bonds but four carbon directions, contradicting equality-implies-sp2.
D3-Q5.probe: Apply the proposed equality-implies-sp2 rule to CH4 and CO2, then compare it with a domain inventory.
D3-Q5.pattern: Four versus two domains refute the shared label. Repeating sp2 solely from equivalence identifies criterion confusion.
D3-Q5.transfer: Write a qualified hybridisation procedure whose inputs exclude bond equivalence as a sufficient test.
D3-Q5.wrong_idea: Bond equivalence by itself implies sp2.

D3-Q6.clarify: Assign each carbon locally and count sigma/pi components across the whole structure.
D3-Q6.connect: A triple bond supplies one sigma plus two pi components.
D3-Q6.way: Number the three carbons; inventory local directions and count every connected atom pair once for sigma.
D3-Q6.rule: Propyne CH3-C≡CH has carbon labels sp3, sp, sp; four C-H plus two C-C sigma bonds gives six sigma, and the triple bond gives two pi.
D3-Q6.check: Independent electron ledger: C3H4 has 16 valence electrons; six sigma pairs plus two pi pairs account for sixteen.
D3-Q6.probe: Count sigma bonds in propyne, then in ethyne. Do double/triple bond lines each count as additional sigma bonds?
D3-Q6.pattern: Propyne six, ethyne three; multiplicity adds pi components. Repeated sigma=line-counting indicates the wrong rule.
D3-Q6.transfer: Classify each carbon and count bond components in ethyne.
D3-Q6.wrong_idea: Each triple-bond line is a sigma bond.

D3-Q7.clarify: Include the terminal-oxygen contributions when describing carbonate pi occupancy.
D3-Q7.connect: Formal charge averages and physical partial charges have different meanings.
D3-Q7.way: Keep sigma/in-plane and perpendicular-p ledgers separate; identify what a contributor average actually averages.
D3-Q7.rule: Carbonate has three in-plane sigma bonds and four perpendicular p functions holding six pi-space electrons. Average formal O charge -2/3 is contributor bookkeeping, not a uniquely measured atomic partial charge.
D3-Q7.check: Independent ledger: CO3^2- has 24 valence electrons; three sigma pairs and six in-plane O lone pairs use eighteen, leaving six in the pi space.
D3-Q7.probe: How many carbonate pi-space electrons arise from one C=O pi pair plus two perpendicular O lone pairs? Does averaging formal charges measure physical partial charges?
D3-Q7.pattern: Six; no. Repeated two-electron count or measured-charge claim exposes the two distinct errors.
D3-Q7.transfer: Explain why equal bond lengths do not uniquely determine atomic partial charges.
D3-Q7.wrong_idea: A delocalised carbonate pi space contains only one pair; formal charge averages are measured partial charges.

D3-Q8.clarify: Separate persistence of the axial sigma connection from claims about all electronic interactions.
D3-Q8.connect: Relative p alignment affects pi overlap; one axial sketch is not a total-energy decomposition.
D3-Q8.way: Rotate relative groups while holding the central bond axis fixed; state only what this model supports.
D3-Q8.rule: Ethane axial C-C sigma bonding can persist through torsion; ethene pi alignment changes under twist. Other interactions, including hyperconjugation, can change; an exclusively steric total-energy account is unjustified.
D3-Q8.check: Changed check: a fixed central sigma direction does not hold every C-H/donor-acceptor orientation fixed.
D3-Q8.probe: During ethane rotation, does an unchanged C-C axis guarantee unchanged orientation of every neighbouring orbital? Compare ethene p alignment.
D3-Q8.pattern: No; ethene relative p alignment also changes. A whole-molecule no-overlap-change claim reveals model overextension.
D3-Q8.transfer: Explain the sigma/pi contrast without assigning a universal torsional energy cause.
D3-Q8.wrong_idea: A fixed central sigma axis means every molecular interaction is unchanged.

D3-Q9.clarify: Trace the continuous aligned p pathway rather than counting all double bonds.
D3-Q9.connect: An intervening saturated sp3 centre breaks the ordinary contiguous pi pathway in this model.
D3-Q9.way: Mark p-bearing centres and inspect adjacency before declaring conjugation.
D3-Q9.rule: Butadiene has four contiguous p-bearing centres; a central saturated CH2 in separated pentadiene interrupts this introductory pathway. This is not a proof of zero interaction of every quantum-mechanical kind.
D3-Q9.check: Changed check: replacing the saturated spacer with an appropriate unsaturated p-bearing centre restores a contiguous path.
D3-Q9.probe: Compare CH2=CH-CH=CH2 with CH2=CH-CH2-CH=CH2. Does spatial closeness alone repair the missing p pathway?
D3-Q9.pattern: No; the first has a continuous path, the second an sp3 interruption. Repeated proximity-based claims reveal the misconception.
D3-Q9.transfer: Specify a structural change that restores the pathway and a model limitation.
D3-Q9.wrong_idea: Spatial closeness repairs an interrupted p pathway.

D3-Q10.clarify: Synthesize a local procedure that also checks inter-centre compatibility.
D3-Q10.connect: Local count, residual p directions and model applicability have different jobs.
D3-Q10.way: Apply the same ordered inventory to each atom, then check neighbouring overlaps; preserve boundaries.
D3-Q10.rule: Count local sigma directions and lone pairs, conserve the valence basis, check residual p orientation and neighbouring compatibility, then qualify applicability. Propyne/allene classifications are atom-local.
D3-Q10.check: Changed check: the procedure must return allene sp2/sp/sp2 and propyne sp3/sp/sp while conserving four carbon basis functions at each site.
D3-Q10.probe: Can a whole molecule have one hybridisation label? Run a local ledger for allene and propyne.
D3-Q10.pattern: No; the positions differ. Repeating one molecule-wide label identifies failure to localise the procedure.
D3-Q10.transfer: State the evidence that would require revisiting a localized lone-pair assignment.
D3-Q10.wrong_idea: A whole molecule has one hybridisation label.

D4-Q1.clarify: Resolve conflict between a local Lewis inventory and supplied aligned delocalisation.
D4-Q1.connect: A hybrid label describes a chosen basis; it does not independently cause donation.
D4-Q1.way: Account for sigma framework, donor orientation and adjacent pi acceptor before qualifying the label.
D4-Q1.rule: Approximately planar amide N can use an introductory sp2-like sigma framework plus an aligned p-like lone-pair donor. Four Lewis entries do not override the supplied delocalised-model conditions; the basis is not unique observed reality.
D4-Q1.check: Remove the hybridisation label: the alignment-plus-acceptor explanation must still describe the supplied donation condition.
D4-Q1.probe: Compare adjacent amide N with a saturated-spacer amine N. Does the same four-entry Lewis inventory establish the same donation pathway?
D4-Q1.pattern: No. Adjacency/alignment conditions differ. Repeating automatic four-domains-therefore-localized-sp3 in both exposes applicability failure.
D4-Q1.transfer: Give one observation that constrains the model and one claim it cannot uniquely prove.
D4-Q1.wrong_idea: Four Lewis entries overrule supplied delocalisation conditions.

D4-Q2.clarify: Construct both arrangements while preserving connectivity and electron inventories.
D4-Q2.connect: Torsion changes relative orientation, not the number of atoms or formal electrons.
D4-Q2.way: Draw a fixed carbonyl reference and an N donor direction rotated about the declared C-N axis.
D4-Q2.rule: Formamide CH3NO has 18 valence electrons and 24 total electrons. The supplied three-centre donor/carbonyl pi model has four electrons. A 90-degree twist changes alignment, not these inventories.
D4-Q2.check: Independent element sums: valence 4+3+5+6=18; total 6+3+7+8=24. Both sketches must preserve them.
D4-Q2.probe: Count valence and total electrons for CH3NO before and after torsion. Identify which geometric relation changes.
D4-Q2.pattern: 18 valence, 24 total in both; relative donor direction changes. Repeated electron-loss-by-rotation reasoning differs from a corrected addition slip.
D4-Q2.transfer: Sketch a fixed-connectivity 45-degree comparison without claiming measured donation.
D4-Q2.wrong_idea: Torsion changes the formal electron inventory.

D4-Q3.clarify: Explain the supplied trend without replacing a mechanism with a label.
D4-Q3.connect: Relative donor/acceptor alignment is a model variable; donation magnitude needs additional physics.
D4-Q3.way: Connect changed geometry to overlap, then tag each statement as given, model or observation.
D4-Q3.rule: Twisting reduces relevant alignment and the supplied delocalisation contribution. A changing hybrid label alone explains neither mechanism nor a quantitative barrier; total torsional energy has additional contributions.
D4-Q3.check: Counterfactual: remove the word hybridisation while retaining changed orientation; the mechanistic statement survives.
D4-Q3.probe: If two sketches have the same label but different donor alignment, must their donation be identical? If the label changes alone, has a mechanism been supplied?
D4-Q3.pattern: Neither follows. Persistent label-only explanations expose causal substitution.
D4-Q3.transfer: State which additional model would be needed for a numerical donation or barrier estimate.
D4-Q3.wrong_idea: A changed hybrid label is a causal explanation of donor strength.

D4-Q4.clarify: Build a decision procedure that can fail its own applicability test.
D4-Q4.connect: Local count and a continuous aligned pathway are independent checks.
D4-Q4.way: Test locality, adjacency, alignment and stated model conditions; invent a structural counterfactual yourself.
D4-Q4.rule: Amide A has the supplied direct donor/carbonyl path. Saturated-spacer amine B lacks that ordinary contiguous path. Spatial proximity alone is insufficient, and absence of this path is not an absolute zero-interaction theorem.
D4-Q4.check: Changed case: replace a saturated interruption by a suitably aligned unsaturated bridge; reassess connectivity and orbital availability rather than reusing the answer.
D4-Q4.probe: Would folding the saturated-spacer molecule closer create the same continuous p pathway as removing the spacer?
D4-Q4.pattern: No; spatial folding and orbital-connected adjacency are different changes. Repeated proximity-based classification identifies the wrong criterion.
D4-Q4.transfer: Specify a counterfactual bridge and test all procedure conditions again.
D4-Q4.wrong_idea: Spatial proximity equals an orbital-connected p pathway.

D4-Q5.clarify: Test uniqueness, rather than merely finding one familiar angle.
D4-Q5.connect: Several shapes/angles can share an introductory four-domain classification.
D4-Q5.way: Use supplied counterexamples and the amide boundary to qualify both predictive scope and evidence.
D4-Q5.rule: CH4/NH3/H2O share common sp3-like introductory descriptions while their nuclear shapes/angles differ. Geometry constrains models but does not uniquely measure a hybrid decomposition; lone pairs and delocalisation matter.
D4-Q5.check: Independent counterexample: a shared four-domain label is compatible with 4,3,2 bonded-atom positions, so it cannot alone uniquely specify atom-only shape.
D4-Q5.probe: Can one four-domain label predict the same nuclear shape for CH4 and H2O? Does observing a shape uniquely establish an orbital basis?
D4-Q5.pattern: No to both. Persistent one-label-one-shape or unique-basis inference reveals overclaim rather than an angle-recall slip.
D4-Q5.transfer: Name evidence needed before claiming a unique physical electronic description.
D4-Q5.wrong_idea: A hybrid label uniquely determines every angle and physical orbital basis.

D4-Q6.clarify: Distinguish recalling a rule from establishing its applicability.
D4-Q6.connect: Local counting assumes the localized/domain model is useful for the asked task.
D4-Q6.way: List the conditions and look for supplied delocalisation or unusual occupancy evidence before applying the shortcut.
D4-Q6.rule: Four-domain counting is useful for localized introductory classification. Adjacent pi acceptors, aligned donor orbitals, planarity/donation evidence or radical occupancy can require a richer model.
D4-Q6.check: Changed check: the same formal lone-pair entry at an amine and an amide can have different orbital-role descriptions under the supplied conditions.
D4-Q6.probe: Both sites have three sigma bonds and a lone pair. Is that alone sufficient to choose identical localized orbital-role descriptions?
D4-Q6.pattern: No; supplied adjacency/alignment evidence differs. Repeated rule use without checking conditions exposes applicability confusion.
D4-Q6.transfer: Separate a recalled count from a model-selection decision in a new conjugated case.
D4-Q6.wrong_idea: Recalling a local rule proves its applicability.

D4-Q7.clarify: Translate occupancy as well as geometry in the supplied radical model.
D4-Q7.connect: A singly occupied orbital is not an empty orbital or a lone pair.
D4-Q7.way: Inventory the sigma electrons and remaining electron before drawing the p-like direction.
D4-Q7.rule: Supplied planar CH3 radical has three sigma directions and a perpendicular p-like SOMO with one electron. Three sigma bonds alone do not determine an empty residual p orbital.
D4-Q7.check: Independent count: CH3 radical has 4+3=7 valence electrons; three sigma pairs use six, leaving one.
D4-Q7.probe: Compare CH3 radical (7 valence electrons) with a model CH3+ inventory (6). Must their residual p occupancy be the same?
D4-Q7.pattern: No: one versus zero in these supplied local models. Repeating empty p for both reveals bonds-only occupancy inference.
D4-Q7.transfer: Sketch the given radical while explicitly marking the singly occupied orbital.
D4-Q7.wrong_idea: Three sigma bonds always imply an empty residual p orbital.

D4-Q8.clarify: Separate a discriminating observation from the strength of the inference it warrants.
D4-Q8.connect: A measurement can constrain multiple models without uniquely selecting an orbital decomposition.
D4-Q8.way: For each proposed observation write prediction, alternatives, conditions and inference limit.
D4-Q8.rule: Planarity/bond metrics and condition-specific spectroscopic/dynamic evidence can test localized versus delocalised accounts. Geometry alone does not uniquely measure donation, hybrid coefficients or a rotational barrier; exact empirical numbers need species/conditions/source.
D4-Q8.check: Use two compatible electronic descriptions of a planar structure as a counterexample to geometry-implies-unique-orbitals.
D4-Q8.probe: Does observed planar geometry alone measure donor strength? What extra information would a numerical rotational barrier require?
D4-Q8.pattern: No; a specified experiment or calculation and conditions/model are needed. Repeating direct geometry-to-strength inference exposes overinterpretation.
D4-Q8.transfer: Design a second independent observation and state one alternative explanation.
D4-Q8.wrong_idea: Geometry alone uniquely measures donation and a rotational barrier.

D4-Q9.clarify: Execute the supplied cosine model and separately test the total-energy inference.
D4-Q9.connect: An overlap factor is not an energy Hamiltonian or the whole energy budget.
D4-Q9.way: Compute the three factors, then identify an independent energy term that the input does not constrain.
D4-Q9.rule: Given factors at 0,60,90 degrees are 1,1/2,0. Both cosine and cosine-squared are even. A degenerate two-orbital Hamiltonian with coupling t0 cos(theta) gives epsilon ± |t0 cos(theta)|, so no universal cosine-squared total-energy law follows.
D4-Q9.check: At theta=60 degrees the factor is fixed at 1/2 while adding an independently specified energy contribution changes total energy. This falsifies uniqueness without modelling formamide quantitatively.
D4-Q9.probe: If theta stays at 60 degrees while an independent energy term changes, does overlap change? Does total energy necessarily stay fixed?
D4-Q9.pattern: Overlap factor unchanged; total energy need not remain fixed. Repeated equality of overlap and total energy identifies variable conflation.
D4-Q9.transfer: State assumptions needed for a weak-coupling second-order squared-interaction estimate.
D4-Q9.wrong_idea: The given overlap factor is the total molecular energy.

D4-Q10.clarify: Audit a proposed universal rule across cases that stress different boundaries.
D4-Q10.connect: Counts, orbital roles, geometry and physical evidence are distinct layers.
D4-Q10.way: Use NH3, allene, amide and separated amine as tests; retain a conditional framework rather than another universal slogan.
D4-Q10.rule: Use local count as a bounded starting model, then check residual p directions, occupancy, adjacency/alignment and evidence. A label alone explains neither every geometry nor all reactivity. NH3, allene and amide stress different limitations.
D4-Q10.check: Changed check: apply the framework to CH3 radical; three bonds plus one unpaired electron require an occupancy step absent from the original slogan.
D4-Q10.probe: Would one bond/lone-pair count plus a label explain NH3 shape, allene terminal-plane relation and amide donation by the same mechanism?
D4-Q10.pattern: No; their explanatory jobs differ. Repeating label-as-final-cause across all cases exposes an overgeneralised framework.
D4-Q10.transfer: Produce a qualified procedure with an explicit stop-and-seek-more-evidence branch.
D4-Q10.wrong_idea: A local count and label explain every geometry and reactivity difference.
